arxiv-2603-21924: Wang and co-authors show that a single heavy metal film can emit terahertz radiation on its own. Metallic terahertz emitters usually pair heavy metals with magnetic layers in spintronic stacks. Working with platinum nanofilms at low temperature under a magnetic field, they trace the emission to the photo-Nernst effect. A fast heat gradient drives a sideways charge current, and the signal flips sign with the Nernst coefficient, as tungsten and tantalum checks confirm. Thinner films and alloying that cut heat conduction both boosted output to spintronic benchmark levels.
arxiv-2603-22324: Yu and co-authors present DAQ, a quantization method that protects what fine-tuning taught a model. Standard quantization shrinks weights to cut reconstruction error. It ignores the base model, so noise can swamp the small weight changes that carry new behavior. DAQ scores quantizers by how well they keep those changes intact. Its two metrics track sign preservation and cosine similarity of the weight deltas. Only the base and tuned weight sets are needed. In an FP8 pilot, DAQ restores style skills that standard quantization erased.
arxiv-2603-22524: Kalaj and Zhu prove a local contraction property for holomorphic functions that are nearly constant. The setting is weighted Bergman spaces on the Bergman ball. Their route turns shape facts about weighted level sets into analytic deficit bounds. A key input is a sharp stability result for the isoperimetric inequality in that ball. Along one special line of exponents, they show the target deficit is controlled by the source deficit. The same bound also measures how far the level sets sit from perfect spheres.
arxiv-2603-22624: Sakib and co-authors ask whether image attribution maps for segmentation tell the truth. A map can look right yet fail to show the pixels that drove the model. The team builds a benchmark that tests faithfulness, off-target credit, stability, and speed. It runs on Pascal VOC and SBD with three pretrained backbones. They also propose Dual-Evidence Attribution, which blends gradient signals with region test results. Where both sources agree, the method gives more credit. It beats gradient-only methods on faithfulness tests, at extra compute cost.
arxiv-2603-22924: Ohlin, Rantzer, and Tegling revisit positive observers for positive linear systems. They show such systems can be stabilized with positive Luenberger-type observers. The observer is built as upper and lower bounds that close in on the state. Closed-loop analysis gives conditions covering a wider class than past designs. The results extend to nonpositive systems via feedback from the upper bound. A stochastic version covers noise as well.
arxiv-2603-23124: Aßbrock, Sperling, and Ares build a frame to spot quantum speedups from polarization. They limit motion to angular momentum coherent states, the classical reference set. A speed limit is computed for change that creates no quantum coherence. Comparing it with the full quantum speed limit isolates the nonclassical gain. Applied to the cross-Kerr interaction, a lasting speedup appears. It grows with the square root of photon number. Even photon counts gain more, they find. Polarization nonclassicality thus acts as a real dynamical resource.
arxiv-2603-23224: Vu and eight co-authors present AeroScene, a diffusion model that builds 3D scenes for drone work. Drone simulators still lean on hand-made scenes, which are slow to build and hard to scale. AeroScene grows scenes in stages, from broad layout down to fine detail. Its hierarchy-aware tokens and multi-branch features keep scenes plausible and consistent. Tests on a new dataset and a public benchmark beat prior methods by a wide margin. The team also releases over 1,000 physics-ready scenes for NVIDIA Isaac Sim.
arxiv-2603-23324: Zhuang and six co-authors present PFGS360, a way to rebuild 3D scenes from 360-degree video without known camera poses. Older Gaussian splatting methods lean on slow structure-from-motion for poses and sparse points. PFGS360 estimates poses through a spherical consistency module. It matches points between the rebuilt Gaussians and raw frames using built-in depth cues. A densification step uses steady depth inliers to grow Gaussians and prune outliers. On real and synthetic 360 videos, it beats prior pose-free and pose-aware methods clearly.
arxiv-2603-23424: Alekseev studies the spectrum of the mixed Hessian of the dispersionless Toda tau function. The Hessian acts as a susceptibility matrix from an inverse conformal map. He works in weighted symmetry-block form on a fixed Hilbert space. The first spectral change hits at an analytic threshold, not the later geometric one where univalence fails. As the threshold nears, each block grows exactly one diverging eigenvalue. The rest of the spectrum stays bounded and settles to a compact limit. Scalar generating functions continue past the threshold as hypergeometric functions.
arxiv-2603-23524: Marcílio-Jr and Eler present Concept Explorer, a system for browsing the concepts inside a language model. Sparse autoencoders split model activity into thousands of readable features. Checking them one by one or by top examples makes wide exploration slow. Their system arranges feature summaries as layered neighborhood maps. Users zoom from broad clusters down to fine local groups. That layout supports finding, comparing, and relating concepts at scale. On SmolLM2 features, it surfaces clean top-level themes and rare concepts that older workflows miss.
arxiv-2603-23624: Maina-Kilaas and Levy test whether hard sentence spots get harder the longer readers stay stuck. Digging-in claims that early structure choices harden over time. Surprisal theory denies the effect unless odds truly shift with length. The pair run two studies on English garden-path sentences with Maze and self-paced reading. They compare readers with a pack of large language models. No real-time digging-in shows up. Apparent gains sit at sentence ends, where wrap-up muddies the read. Mid-sentence items trend the other way.
arxiv-2603-24124: Liu measures an alignment tax in language models tuned with human feedback. On TruthfulQA, 40 to 79 percent of questions yield a single semantic cluster across ten samples. On those questions, sampling-based uncertainty methods lose all power to separate right from wrong. Token entropy still carries some signal. A base-versus-instruct test pins the cause on alignment, and a stage test blames DPO, not SFT. Effects vary by model family and size. A cheap cascade of uncertainty signals lifts selective prediction scores in tests.
arxiv-2603-24224: Mayumu and co-authors present RVLM, a vision-language system for medical images that reasons in steps. Normal models answer in one pass, which hides their logic from clinicians. RVLM instead loops: it writes Python code, calls vision sub-agents, edits images, and gathers evidence. Each claim rests on code that can be audited. A router sets how many steps to take and stops early when progress stalls. Tests use brain MRI from BraTS 2023 and chest X-rays from MIMIC-CXR, with no fine-tuning.
arxiv-2603-24524: Schiller and co-authors set out a way to judge methods that assign a model's uncertainty to input features. Studies of such methods use mismatched proxy tasks and metrics, so results cannot be compared. The authors align the task with the Co-12 scheme and give measures for four traits: correctness, consistency, continuity, and compactness. They add a fifth trait, conveyance, which checks if set rises in uncertainty reach the feature scores. Across eight metrics, gradient methods beat perturbation ones on consistency and conveyance.
arxiv-2603-25024: Yu and Fang speed up infinitely deep Bayesian neural networks with a classic optimizer trick. These networks rest on stochastic differential equations, which give strong theory but cost many solver steps. Each step means a fresh function pass, so training and testing run slow and can wobble. The team adds Nesterov's accelerated gradient into the model, plus a skip link whose strength depends on step count. Their model settles faster and needs far fewer passes. Across image and sequence tasks, it beats standard versions on both cost and accuracy.
arxiv-2603-25324: Malakar and Ghosh map the topological phases of polyacene, a ribbon-like organic polymer. They build seven tight-binding models across the cis and trans shapes plus five reshaped variants. Band patterns for cis and trans look the same, yet their topology is opposite. The trans form carries a nonzero winding number, while cis stays trivial. Oddly, both hold the symmetries their class seems to need; a mirror rule sets them apart. Tweaked variants host flat band pairs. Each model's topological character turns out distinct.
arxiv-2603-25524: Chan and co-authors release CHIRP, a dataset for tracking wild birds as individuals over years. It follows Siberian jays in Swedish Lapland, a population studied long term. The set supports five vision jobs: re-identification, action naming, pose keypoints, detection, and segmentation. Scores also use biology-grade measures like feeding and co-presence rates. Their CORVID pipeline names birds by the color rings on their legs. It beats top re-identification methods on the real-use scores. The pair offers a template for field datasets.
arxiv-2603-27024: Griss Salas and King propose a structured neural ODE for learning multistable systems from data. Many engineered processes settle into one of several equilibria set by control inputs. Stable data excites the system weakly, so plain model discovery is ill-posed. Their architecture builds stability in: a negative factor forces contraction toward an equilibrium map. That map directly encodes where the multiple attractors sit. Short training runs captured several basins of attraction in benchmarks. The equilibrium map also enables fast gradient-based feedback control design.
arxiv-2603-27524: Ferdous and co-authors compare breaking changes in human and AI pull requests. The study covers 7,191 agent-made and 1,402 human-made requests. All come from Python projects in the AIDev dataset. A syntax-tree tool flags likely breaking changes in each diff. Agents break compatibility less often overall than humans. Rates land at 3.45 versus 7.40 percent in code tasks. But agents show much higher rates in some task types. The full report maps where each risk concentrates.
arxiv-2603-27624: Ma and co-authors speed up mixture-of-experts inference on chiplet hardware. Edge use means small batches and tight on-chip memory. Expert loads also swing sharply at runtime. Their FSE-DP plan shards experts fully across chiplets. Fine streams of expert work follow dynamic paths. High die-to-die bandwidth carries those streams. Simple virtualization rules tame the dataflow. A light scheduler keeps loads balanced. Gains reach about 1.22 times in their tests.
arxiv-2603-28024: Wan and Yang study two-dimensional hydroelastic Stokes waves in water of infinite depth. They first justify a focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation as an approximation for the full wave system. They then use the known instability of that equation to prove a stronger claim. The Stokes waves themselves are nonlinearly unstable under long-wave perturbations. The proof links the simple model's behavior to the real fluid system.
arxiv-2603-28324: Katz and three co-authors generate new 3D organ shapes with a stochastic method built on shape registration. Their framework learns the drift between geometries through large deformation mapping, then works on curved domains rather than flat grids. For blood-flow studies, they grow fresh aorta shapes from a patient group, guided by centerline points and sphere radii. The tool can also nudge a given shape by a set amount. That helps measure how scan errors affect key flow markers.
arxiv-2603-28924: Bouras introduces CrossTrace, a dataset of grounded reasoning traces for scientific hypothesis generation. Past datasets cover single domains and lack explicit reasoning steps. CrossTrace holds 1,389 traces across biomedical research, AI and ML, and cross-domain work. Each trace links prior knowledge through logical steps to a new hypothesis, grounded in source text. A schema adds step level verification and eight discovery patterns. Fine-tuning a Qwen model on the data raised judged scores and structural compliance sharply. Human checks of 150 records found 99.7 percent step level grounding accuracy and no fabrication.
arxiv-2603-29224: Wang and Zhang ask what training data a neural PDE simulator should keep under a tight budget. Coarsening and quantization can erase fine-scale detail before training starts. Their analysis uses periodic incompressible Navier-Stokes flow. Quantization error hits the finest retained band hardest. Velocity and vorticity also distort in different ways. Their method, DerivOpt, picks which fields to carry and at what precision. On PDEBench, it cut fine-band error and rollout error.
arxiv-2603-29424: Lyon develops a proof-search method for intuitionistic tense logics. The method uses nested sequents and supports finite counter-model extraction. A new loop check spots repeating sequents through homomorphisms. That check bounds how tall derivations can grow during search. Some rules are not invertible, so search builds a computation tree instead of one derivation. Proofs come out when search succeeds. Counter-models come out when it fails. This proves the finite model property for a family of these logics.
arxiv-2603-29524: Mangioni and Tesolin extend the Milnor-Schwarz lemma to inverse monoids. The classic lemma links group actions on metric spaces with algebraic structure. Their version covers inverse monoids acting on presheaves of geodesic metric spaces. They give two proofs of the generalization. The first uses only elementary tools, modeled on the group action arguments. The second uses a form of the Vietoris-Rips complex. That proof builds on work by Chung, Martínez, and Szakács. The note sits in geometric inverse semigroup theory.
arxiv-2603-29724: Breaz and co-authors tackle the cost of estimating rare event chances with many random inputs. They extend a Kriging-based active subspace method into a sequential version. The method re-fits its low-dimensional view until that view settles. Tests show lower prediction error and a better subspace fit. They then plug it into a rare event method that learns an importance sampling density. Results show a precise estimate at lower cost.
arxiv-2603-29824: Zheng and Proutière tackle the gap between LoRA tuning and full fine-tuning of large models. Matching parameter updates only shapes predictions indirectly. They instead pose a prediction alignment problem in function space. Its best low-rank updates look like a curvature-whitened Newton step. Their CG-LoRA method picks directions from local curvature data. It avoids building large second-order matrices. On standard language benchmarks, it converges faster and beats other LoRA variants.
arxiv-2603-29924: Lu and co-authors present Abstraction in Style, a method for artistic style transfer. Real styles rework structure, not just texture and color. Older transfer methods keep the input geometry, so they miss that deeper change. Their AiS first builds an abstraction proxy from a target image and style samples. The proxy recasts structure while loosening geometric fidelity. A second stage renders the proxy into the final image. Both stages learn from visual examples alone.
arxiv-2604-00024: Maurya and team present WHBench, a test suite of 47 scenarios across 10 women's health topics, exposing failure modes like outdated guidelines and dosing errors. Language models now serve medical guidance, but women's health remains neglected. The team evaluates 22 models with a 23-criterion rubric for accuracy, safety, clarity, equity, and guideline following, with safety-weighted penalties. Across 3,102 responses, no model mean exceeds 75 percent; the best reaches 72.1 percent. Even leading models show low fully correct rates and wide variation in harm rates. Raters mostly agree on labels and on ranking.
arxiv-2604-00524: Daráš and colleagues compare two data based predictive controllers on a pasteurisation unit. Both offer the constraint handling and optimisation of predictive control with no physics model, but they swap the model out. One method, data-enabled predictive control, forecasts from input and output runs using Hankel matrices. The other, Koopman control, learns a lifted state space model from data. Tests on multivariable process control are rare. The team runs both on one unit with three hand-set inputs and three measured outputs, sharing horizons, cost weights, and constraints.
arxiv-2604-00624: Apollonio and colleagues study the critical patch size in graphs. Critical patch size is a threshold for habitats to persist. They are graphs with a set of nodes acting as sinks. Sinks impose edge rules akin to Dirichlet conditions in smooth domains. Groups grow at nodes and diffuse through the graph Laplacian, but cannot survive in sinks. The Dirichlet value of the habitat is the value of the Laplacian block after dropping sink rows and columns. It governs whether they live: they live when it falls below a set ratio.
arxiv-2604-00724: Maus, Nolin, and Schager design faster deterministic algorithms for balanced orientations and degree splits in distributed computing. Their method runs in time proportional to the inverse of the error tolerance times the logarithm of network size, improving on an earlier bound. The same approach also yields undirected splits of degrees with equal discrepancy and running time.
arxiv-2604-00924: Ren and Huang connect the superconformal index of N=4 U(N) super Yang-Mills to the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Schneider integrable system. The index can be written with elliptic Macdonald polynomials, giving a compact sum over generalized partitions from structure constants and normalization constants. Solving the Ruijsenaars-Schneider model stepwise in the elliptic parameter p yields an expansion of the index as powers of p. They check that in a deformed one-half BPS limit, and most of all in the large N limit, their formalism reduces to known results.
arxiv-2604-01024: Jordan and Kamgarpour study model learning of finite-window policies in POMDPs. Finite windows stand in for endless past links, a finite process from pasts, the superstate MDP. With a superstate model, methods can compute optimal policies, but gauging is hard because runs come from the first process, not the target model. They propose a gauging method for tabular POMDPs and study its sample needs via filter stability and concentration inequalities. From a single run, they get tight bounds, yielding near-optimal finite-window policies with value iteration.
arxiv-2604-01124: Zoufaly and colleagues present a control setup for shoulder-blade and upper-arm rhythm, pairing a quaternion model with muscle-signal tuning. The setup drops motion break points and glitches seen in the Euler-angle model, while keeping accuracy. Muscle-signal tuning cuts gaps between forecast and measured muscle firings by up to 60% on test tasks. In model runs setting only arm lifts, shoulder-blade and collarbone motion emerge from muscle physics and effort saving, giving matching rhythm values. Rotator cuff weakness shifts work to shoulder-joint turning.
arxiv-2604-01224: Yoo and colleagues introduce SoftAct, a framework that teaches soft robot hands human-like manipulation by reasoning explicitly about contact forces. Immersive virtual reality captures human demos, including hand motion, object motion, dense contact patches, and detailed force data. A two-stage retargeting algorithm first assigns demo forces to human fingers and allocates robot fingers in proportion, then refines fingertip targets online using contact geometry and force size. Tests on a custom pneumatic soft hand show fingertip tracking error falls by up to 55 percent.
arxiv-2604-01324: Ganguly and colleagues attack the primordial lithium problem with a two-stage decay story that also respects tight deuterium limits. First a majoron decaying mainly to neutrinos raises neutron numbers and lowers lithium-7 plus beryllium-7, but pushes deuterium too high. Then an axion-like particle decaying to photons trims the deuterium excess through late photodissociation without undoing the lithium drop. The setup is model-dependent, but it proves such correlated abundance shifts can work.
arxiv-2604-01624: Shah and colleagues define commitment uncertainty localization: from a denoising run, flag tokens whose cross-chain entropy exceeds an unsupervised threshold. They also introduce OSCAR, a training-free runtime method using this idea. OSCAR runs N noise chains with shuffled reveals, computes cross-chain Shannon entropy to flag spots, and does targeted remasking using retrieved evidence. On TriviaQA, HotpotQA, RAGTruth, and CommonsenseQA with LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B, OSCAR cuts hallucinated content and lifts factual accuracy through uncertainty-led masking. Its native entropy signal beats trained detectors.
arxiv-2604-01724: Chowdhury and colleagues build a framework forcing full synchronization in bi-harmonic Sakaguchi-Kuramoto oscillator networks, where phase frustration usually blocks sync. They derive frequencies, robust to noise and tied to uneven node degrees, plus coupling settings that yield full sync. In scale-free networks the transition shows hysteresis, a first-order jump, while Erdős-Rényi networks sync through a second-order transition. Mean-field analysis gives the coupling for the second-harmonic case, with a two-cluster state. The findings hold across varied networks.
arxiv-2604-01824: Bahrami and colleagues present STRIVE, a reinforcement learning framework for video question answering. Group-based policy methods suffer low reward spread when answers are alike, giving weak advantage estimates. STRIVE builds several versions of each video and scales jointly across text outputs and visual versions, widening contrasts to visual changes. A sampling step favors frames most apt for the question while keeping time coverage. Tests on six video benchmarks show steady gains over strong rivals across large models.
arxiv-2604-01924: El Khettari and colleagues ask whether clinical notes can forecast short term death in heart failure, testing text, structured records and combined models in French patients. Entity detail in the notes beat plain whole-note embeddings, and supervised fusion of text with structured variables gave the best scores. Large language models behaved unevenly across inputs and decoding choices, with prompts using text alone ahead of structured or combined inputs. The verdict favors combined transformers tracking entities, while prompt-driven language models still fall short as clinical aids.
arxiv-2604-02324: Chen and colleagues fix how new vocabulary tokens start life in language models for recommendation. Standard practice sets each new token to the mean of existing embeddings. Spectral and geometric checks show this collapses new tokens into a degenerate subspace, erasing distinctions fine tuning struggles to recover. Their GTI stage grounds each new token at a distinct, meaningful spot in the pretrained space using paired linguistic supervision. Grounded tokens beat mean starts and auxiliary task methods on most generative recommendation benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-02424: Hasenfratz and Xu set general rules for symmetric mass generation and test their fit with lattice QCD. They propose RG flow paths near the transition and argue meson mass ratio can probe it as a UV fixed point. Goldstone four quark meson states are named as signs of the type II phase.
arxiv-2604-02724: Nguyen investigates a distributed optimal control problem for the viscous Camassa-Holm equations. The controls are sparse, and the cost functional is broad. The problem spans a region, not one point. Looking at three different sparsity-promoting terms, he proves that optimal solutions exist. He derives the matching optimality conditions. He also studies how stable the optimal solutions are when the sparsity parameter changes.
arxiv-2604-02824: Stellhorn and twelve colleagues find disorder-induced chirality in superconductor-ferromagnet hybrids through neutron scattering and multi-scale models. In FePd and Nb/FePd structures they observe partial order, mixing, anti-phase boundaries, and a defect gradient, plus finite net magnetic chirality at room temperature. Theory shows chemical disorder with a compositional gradient creates Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions. Those interactions hold steady chiral ripples of mixed Bloch-Néel form. The main chiral contribution sits in-plane, with a smaller out-of-plane part.
arxiv-2604-03224: Liu and colleagues unify chest CT analysis so one system can handle lung checks and opportunistic screening beyond the lungs. Their HyperCT framework adapts a vision transformer backbone through a hypernetwork, using low-rank updates instead of full parameters for each task. Tested on a large radiology and cardiology dataset, it beats strong baselines while staying parameter-efficient for whole-patient assessment.
arxiv-2604-03324: Higuchi asks where finite MV-effect algebras first fail when the sequential-product axioms are weakened one by one. He shows the fourth axiom is the first fatal one. Any algebra with an atom whose finite isotropic index reaches at least two admits no operation meeting the first four axioms. A finite MV-effect algebra therefore admits one exactly when it is Boolean. He also classifies lower-axiom operations by matrices, counting exactly 34 on the rank-two Boolean algebra.
arxiv-2604-03424: Nelson, Grest, and Olmsted compare polymer-melt shear runs against a model linking tube motion to entanglement motion via flow-driven constraint release. The model predicts shear banding once the resting entanglement number passes a critical value set by a release parameter. Runs agree roughly, with gaps blamed on model shortcuts and tube models failing for partly freed liquids in strong flow.
arxiv-2604-03724: Ben Kabongo and colleagues argued that a system should pick its reasons for a suggestion from a ranked list, rather than writing them up from scratch. Their StaR approach ranks short candidate lines drawn from user reviews and returns the best ones as the reason. That curbs made-up claims and lets each claim be checked on its own. Each line must say something real, cover one point only, and not repeat another line. Simple popularity baselines proved surprisingly strong when ranked per item.
arxiv-2604-03824: Adrián Antón-Álvarez and Adrián Lozano-Durán released HYMOR, an open-source toolkit for stability analysis of high-enthalpy hypersonic flows. It covers global modal, non-modal, and freestream receptivity analysis, catching interactions between distant mechanisms that local methods miss. A shock-fitting treatment keeps the bow shock sharp, and several thermochemical models handle real-gas effects. Benchmark tests verified the MATLAB and Julia implementations across all three analysis modes.
arxiv-2604-03924: Xinyi Ling and colleagues treated goal-oriented conversation as uncertainty-aware planning across multiple turns. Structured methods plan well but need fixed schemas, while language-model methods flex but lack long-horizon decisions. Their CUP framework lets a language model propose actions and a planner weigh their long-term effect on uncertainty. Tests on several conversational benchmarks showed higher success with fewer turns, plus faster information gathering and earlier confident commitment.
arxiv-2604-04324: Bhat and colleagues tackle remaking the computer models behind control-systems papers, where missing parameters and vague details block reruns. They define Paper to Simulation Recoverability: whether a system can write working code that matches a paper's results. Their RESCORE setup pairs three agents, Analyzer, Coder and Verifier, using run feedback and visual checks to sharpen the match. On a 500-paper IEEE control-conference test set, RESCORE remakes matching simulations for 40.7 percent of cases, beating one-pass tries. The machine pipeline runs about ten times faster than manual reruns.
arxiv-2604-04924: Rajagopalan and Patel show that a pre-trained diffusion model already knows how to restore images, without fine-tuning or added control modules. That hidden ability can be unlocked by learning prompt embeddings at the output of the text encoder, though plain text prompts and token-embedding tuning barely reach it. Naive prompt learning proves unstable, since forward noising from degraded images misaligns with reverse sampling. Training prompts inside a diffusion bridge formulation aligns the two paths, releasing all-in-one restoration from the frozen model.
arxiv-2604-05024: Zhang and 19 co-authors test whether star formation histories of massive quiescent galaxies match their rapid number density evolution since redshift about seven. They appear in early JWST data far above most theory. The team models JWST NIRCam images and NIRSpec spectra of massive quiet galaxies at redshift two to five from the RUBIES survey, using stellar population models and Bayesian fitting with Prospector. They infer star formation pasts and test how results shift with model sets and history choices, asking whether implied counts match seen growth.
arxiv-2604-05224: Berman and three colleagues give AttriBench, the first even quote credit benchmark. Evening out fame and groups enables fair study of group bias in credit. Across prompt settings, 11 widely used models still struggle with credit, with large score gaps between race, gender, and mixed groups. They also study silence, where models omit credit fully despite access to writer info. Silence is common and uneven across groups, showing biases missed by standard score metrics.
arxiv-2604-05324: Aiyer, Mansour, Moran, and Shao ask which scores for generative models can actually be trusted when judged from finite test samples. Error rates for classifiers are well understood, but open-ended generation makes evaluation murkier. Their framework shows that integral probability metrics, which compare models through a bounded family of test functions, can be estimated from samples within combined error bounds. Renyi and KL divergences fail that test, the authors prove, because rare events can swing their values.
arxiv-2604-05624: Falola and five colleagues build YoNER, a multi-domain Yorùbá named-entity dataset of about 5,000 sentences and 100,000 tokens across Bible, blogs, movies, radio, and Wikipedia. Three native speakers annotated persons, organizations, and locations with agreement above 0.70. African-centered models beat general multilingual ones, but cross-domain scores fall sharply, and the team releases YoNER plus a new OyoBERT model.
arxiv-2604-05724: Ro, Choi, and Kim add information scope to sparse-autoencoder analysis of CLIP vision encoders, asking how broadly each feature pools visual evidence. Their Contextual Dependency Score separates stable local features from shifting global ones. Scope shapes predictions and confidence systematically, giving a new diagnostic axis beyond feature meaning, and suggesting scope-aware checks for future interpretability work.
arxiv-2604-06024: In their 2026 paper, Liu and three colleagues frame the risk of cascading failures in time-delay consensus networks. Agents meeting on a shared schedule despite disturbances and delays motivate the work. Average value-at-risk measures cascading uncertainty system-wide. Closed-form expressions link failure risk to the network's Laplacian spectrum, delay, and noise statistics. Lower bounds mark the best delay-limited performance. They serve as feasibility certificates for safety and performance goals. A single-step update law spreads conditional risk as failures appear.
arxiv-2604-06424: Grazhdanski, Vassileva, Koychev, and Boytcheva present a transformer-based approach to the SympTEMIST named entity recognition and entity linking tasks. For named entity recognition, they tune a RoBERTa-based token classifier with BiLSTM and CRF layers on extra training data. For entity linking, candidates come from cross-lingual SapBERT XLMR-Large, ranked by cosine similarity against a knowledge base. Knowledge base choice most affects model accuracy.
arxiv-2604-06624: Zhao and Zhao model how data-center power delivery can shake the grid. Unlike legacy industrial loads, data centers use power-electronic interfaces whose multi-timescale dynamics can excite oscillations. Their explicit, component-informed model keeps component-level detail and captures control interactions between stages, cast as a time-invariant positive-sequence representation. That form plugs into standard phasor-domain grid models, and case studies show how server-load swings at certain frequencies amplify and spread oscillations across grids with mixed resources.
arxiv-2604-06724: Angmalisang and Neumann add time windows to the traveling thief problem, where goods can only be picked up at set times. The problem already joins routing with packing, and real delivery jobs demand such timing limits. They adapt existing thief-problem and traveling-salesperson methods to the timed variant, add a new heuristic of their own, and build fresh benchmark instances from literature cases. Tests across many instances show their new algorithm beating the adapted rivals on a wide range.
arxiv-2604-06824: Park and Kim localize sound sources without training, using multimodal models that reason about their own work. Most sound-source finding leans on contrastive matching, lacking explicit checks in complex noisy scenes. Their three-stage pipeline first generates boxes and audio labels, then scores audio-visual consistency through open-set role tagging and anchor voting, and finally gates tweaks on the fly to avoid extra changes. Trials on single-source and multi-source benchmarks show competitive results, with code shared.
arxiv-2604-07324: Sanders proves a quantitative version of the Beurling-Helson theorem about maps of the circle to itself. If a continuous map has Fourier algebra norms growing no faster than a small power of log, with exponent one eighth minus any positive epsilon, then the map must be affine linear. That is, it takes the form of an integer multiple of the input plus a constant shift. The result sharpens the classical rigidity claim by giving an explicit growth threshold that forces this rigid form.
arxiv-2604-07424: Nananukul and Kejriwal survey AI use across 58746 NIH projects from 2025, sorting research texts with a human-checked language-model method. AI covers 15.9 percent of the portfolio with a 13.4 percent funding premium, focused on discovery, prediction, and data integration. Yet most AI work stays in research: 79 percent, with just 14.7 percent reaching clinical use. Health disparities work is scarce at 5.7 percent of AI funding, despite its key role in NIH equity goals.
arxiv-2604-07624: Desai and three colleagues present PAGENT, a scalable approach to generating proof-of-concept inputs that trigger reported software vulnerabilities. Given project source code and a suspect code location, PAGENT blends lightweight rule-based static analysis with sanitizer-based profiling and coverage data to guide a generation agent. Symbolic execution and fuzzing need expert guidance and manual steps and scale poorly, while plain language-model generation succeeds rarely. In experiments, the hybrid approach beats the prior top agentic approach by 132 percent on proof-of-concept generation.
arxiv-2604-07924: Dutta and Bhalekar study how chaos arises in a simple model with two time delays. In their delay differential equation, the present rate of change depends on the current state and on past states at two distinct delay times. The delays encode memory effects, while sine terms inject strong nonlinearity. Numerical simulations explore behavior across parameter values. Chaotic motion is identified with Lyapunov exponents, Poincaré maps, power spectrum analysis, and phase portraits, which together reveal irregular motion that never settles into a simple repeating pattern.
arxiv-2604-08224: Zhou and 20 colleagues review externalization in LLM agents: memory, skills, protocols, and harness engineering. Large language model agents are built less by changing weights than by reorganizing their runtime. Capabilities once expected from the model now live outside it, in memory stores, reusable skills, interaction protocols, and harness engineering. The review looks at this shift via externalization. Drawing on cognitive artifacts, the authors argue infrastructure matters because it turns hard cognitive burdens into forms the model handles more reliably. Here, memory externalizes state across time.
arxiv-2604-08324: Léger, Meidani, and Gagné analyze alignment in latent space tuning for multi-modal learning. Symbolic regression finds math expressions from data, traditionally tackled with genetic programming via combinatorial search. Latent Space Optimization maps symbolic expressions into vector spaces with neural encoders, turning search into smooth tuning. SNIP, a contrastive pre-training model after CLIP, advances latent space tuning with a multi-modal approach, aligning symbol and numeric nets in one latent space. Numeric-space tuning then implicitly guides symbol search. However, this needs fine-grained cross-modal alignment.
arxiv-2604-08424: Capelli and ten colleagues make fault finding on self driving satellites easier to trust and explain. Their peephole method pulls small, labeled encodings out of a neural anomaly detector's middle layers, applied here to a convolutional autoencoder watching reaction wheel telemetry. The labeled signals pinpoint and locate faults, expose detector bias, and add only a small computing cost, keeping the approach feasible aboard a satellite.
arxiv-2604-08524: Cheng, Wiegreffe, and Manocha ask what steering vectors actually change inside language models, using refusal as a test case. A multi token activation patching study finds varied steering methods use interchangeable circuits at the same layer, acting mainly via the OV circuit and largely bypassing the QK circuit. Freezing attention scores costs little performance, and steering vectors can be cut by 85 to 96 percent while keeping most of their effect.
arxiv-2604-08624: Abdennadher and Garner bring Bayesian learning to spiking neural networks for speech, smoothing their jagged predictive landscape. Threshold based spike generation makes predictions angular and irregular, but a Bayesian treatment of weights, including the efficient IVON variational method, yields smoother landscapes. Tests on Heidelberg Digits and Speech Commands improve negative log likelihood and Brier score, with one dimensional weight slices confirming the smoother landscape.
arxiv-2604-09024: Shao and three colleagues defend personal images against misuse by open-weight multimodal models, which can extract identities, locations, and other private details at scale. Their ImageProtector method works on the user's side, embedding a protective perturbation into images before sharing, aiming to shield them from large-scale automated analysis. The paper tests three countermeasures, Gaussian noise, DiffPure, and adversarial training, and finds they only partly blunt the defense. Those countermeasures also degrade model accuracy or efficiency, showing both the promise and the limits of perturbation-based privacy protection.
arxiv-2604-09124: Russo and eight colleagues present MATCHA, a unified system for running deep neural networks on edge chips with multiple mixed speedup engines. Most systems cannot fully exploit such mix. MATCHA builds highly joint plans for mixed engines and uses constraint code to tune memory sharing and timing across levels. Pattern matching, tiling, and mapping across single hardware units enable side-by-side runs. The system targets lean use on multi-engine mixed edge systems-on-chip.
arxiv-2604-09224: Dupont and six colleagues investigate many-body dynamical localization in the Fock space of a driven two-mode bosonic system, mapped onto the kicked-top model. Classical mean-field motion spreads in a bounded ergodic way along the population imbalance axis. Quantum interference, by contrast, strongly suppresses transport, much like Anderson localization in disordered lattices. They characterize the localization length, its scaling with particle number and driving settings, and a spectral crossover from random-matrix to Poisson statistics as the ensemble localizes.
arxiv-2604-09324: Su, Hongsong Wang, Gui, and Liang Wang propose structure-aware fine-grained Gaussian splatting for expressive avatars from monocular video. Existing avatar methods capture body motion but often miss fine details like hand movements and facial expressions. Their SFGS method uses a spatial-only triplane and a time-aware hexplane to capture dynamic features across frames, plus a module for pose-dependent details. A refinement module targets hand deformations, and single-stage training beats baselines, producing high-fidelity avatars with natural motion.
arxiv-2604-09524: Costello and four colleagues model lunar regolith gardening as impact-driven advection against diffusion. It matches Apollo core age patterns from 14 million to 450 million years. It fits the depth pattern of live iron-60 in Apollo samples. That fit suggests supernova dust arrives independently of native iron. The model also predicts signals for heavy r-process species such as plutonium-244. Comparing plutonium and iron profiles could reveal plutonium's origin and guide Artemis sampling to about 100 centimeters.
arxiv-2604-09624: Hedna and three colleagues tackle language-model overconfidence with SECL, a test-time training pipeline that needs no labeled data. A model's token probability for True, when asked whether its answer is right, is better calibrated than its stated confidence. SECL turns that gap into label-free self-supervision, adapting only when inputs shift and training on just 6 to 26 percent of questions. Across four models from three families and four domains, it cuts expected calibration error by 56 to 78 percent, beating its own supervision signal.
arxiv-2604-09724: Kambiré fleshes out a sketch by Krachun and Kazanin proving that proximity gaps fail for a certain family of Reed-Solomon codes near capacity. The gaps fail at radii on the order of one over log n below the code's capacity rate, where n is the code length. Proximity gaps concern how close a received word must sit to the code for list-decoding guarantees to hold, so their failure near capacity marks a boundary for those guarantees. The report works out the sketch in full for this code family.
arxiv-2604-09824: Darabi and Trivedi present ProGAL-VLA, tackling language ignorance, where vision-language-action models use visual shortcuts and ignore instruction changes. ProGAL-VLA builds a 3D entity graph, plans sub-goals slowly, and matches them to grounded entities through a contrastive loss. All actions use a goal embedding whose attention entropy signals ambiguity. On LIBERO-Plus, robustness rises from about 30 percent to about 72 percent, and entity retrieval lifts from about four tenths to about seven tenths. On Custom Ambiguity, clarification rises from about a tenth to about four fifths.
arxiv-2604-09924: Chum and three co-authors build S3CDM, a detector for large organizations' networks, aimed at insider attacks. The model splits a secret among legitimate participants for authentication, using Shamir interpolation and a hash-based scheme. Both schemes keep component communications secure and flag unauthorized activity, with flexible multi-factor authentication strengthening security. Analysis shows the multi-component model resists attacks better than a single-component one. The team implements S3CDM on Google Cloud Platform in three parts: interface, services, and database, demonstrated with a broken-path simulation.
arxiv-2604-10324: Vavitsas, Wu, and Zarvalis examine the cycling threshold for functions in Dirichlet-type spaces. For a fixed key index, they construct a smooth function that is cycling for every index below the key index but fails to be cycling at the key index itself. The function serves as a counter-case to survival of cycling at the key index. The build uses broad Cantor sets and studies their Riesz size, linking cycling ways to the shape of these sets.
arxiv-2604-10424: Wang and six colleagues test whether heart signal encoders leak who trained them. Shared ECG encoders hand out scores or hidden vectors, which foes can probe for membership clues. Their audit hits contrastive and masked rebuild encoders through three realistic attacker routes. Leaks run worst in small or single site groups and can saturate in hidden vector space. Wider, mixed data sets blunt the tail risk, so hiding raw waves alone cannot guard enrollment privacy.
arxiv-2604-10624: Kania and Niwiński define norm-controlled semiprojectivity for Banach lattices. It requires lattice maps to lift through limits of closed ideals with only small norm loss. Their main result: C(X) is semiprojective exactly when the compact metric space X is an absolute neighbourhood retract. This beats the C*-algebra case, where dimension at most one is also required. Uncountable sums of certain projective lattices are semiprojective but need not be projective, while lp, Lp, and Orlicz spaces are not.
arxiv-2604-10724: Lin and Zeldes test how entity salience in discourse relates to surprisal, the information load of a word, using 70,000 annotated mentions across 16 genres of English. Salient entities carry significantly higher surprisal than non-salient ones, even after controlling for position, length, and nesting. Salient entities also lower surprisal for surrounding content when used as prompts, sharpening predictability. The effect varies by genre, strongest in topic-coherent texts and weakest in conversation. The findings refine the uniform-information-density framework by naming global salience as a force shaping information distribution.
arxiv-2604-10824: Ai splits the gap in high school STEM results tied to ADHD status into direct, indirect, and spurious parts, using national data from the High School Longitudinal Study of 2009. For overall STEM grades, the ADHD penalty is large: total variation of minus 0.670, with 63.3 percent of it direct, acting outside seen social or school factors. For science identity, the gap is small and not significant, at minus 0.068. The direct effect also shifts by race and ethnicity, and checks show it holds up under modest hidden bias.
arxiv-2604-11224: Goyal, Arora, and Goel make Community Notes, the crowdsourced fact-checking program on X, harder to sway. Its matrix factorization model separates ideology from note quality, but then treats all raters alike, slowing consensus and leaving quality open to noisy or strategic raters. Their quality-sensitive variant gives more weight to raters whose ideology-adjusted ratings match the learned quality, needing 26 to 40 percent fewer ratings on high-traffic notes and resisting coordinated attacks better.
arxiv-2604-11924: Mun and four colleagues study scientific paper feedback that authors actually act on, using author responses as success signals. They curate GoodPoint-ICLR: 19,000 ICLR papers with reviewer feedback annotated for validity and author action. Their GoodPoint training recipe fine-tunes on valid, actionable feedback and adds preference optimisation on real and synthetic pairs. On a 1,200-paper benchmark, a GoodPoint-trained Qwen3-8B lifts predicted success by 83.7 percent over its base model and tops similar-size models on matching golden human feedback, even beating Gemini-3-flash on precision.
arxiv-2604-12124: Kresin and three colleagues develop causal inference for space-time event outcomes under cell treatments with outcome spillover. Post-treatment events mix latent control and treatment parts that cannot be told apart. Expected counts under a given treatment plan are identified under consistency, exchangeability, and positivity. Fitting uses stochastic EM, with guarantees for local and global effects. The framework covers history-dependent processes such as Poisson and Hawkes models, with uses in epidemiology, seismology, and finance. A test case looks at wastewater injection effects on Oklahoma quakes.
arxiv-2604-12324: Batra and two colleagues present HICM, a framework for harmonizing Indian census migration data across three decades of records. The data suffer gaps from uneven coverage and inconsistent measurement across states and time, distorting later analysis. It corrects two bias types before analysis, using careful preprocessing and checks grounded in statistics. Bias-aware fixes greatly improve data consistency and the reliability of later temporal results, supporting policy-relevant long-run network analysis.
arxiv-2604-13124: Kato, Onozaki, Saiki, and Sugita study iterated function systems that switch at random between two different 1D maps, simple models of regime-switching dynamics. They derive exact parameter rules for finite invariant sets with toss-and-catch dynamics, where paths alternate between fixed and periodic points. Two routes emerge: bridging points linking invariant structures of different maps, and real overlaps shared by the maps, with bridging points that are periodic points of neither map.
arxiv-2604-13624: Xiang and ten colleagues assess NOR-type IGZO FeFETs for read-heavy artificial intelligence memory, spanning on-chip RAM, bonded chiplets, and stacked storage-class memory. Their co-optimization shows bitcells shrinking to a 10-ampere SRAM-equivalent area with sub-5-nanosecond access, despite writing difficulties. They also flag a sensing penalty from sneak current tied to negative threshold voltage, which positive-threshold engineering can remove.
arxiv-2604-14124: Yunerman, Price, and Öberg model how ices enrich in evolving planet-forming disks. Before about half a million years, drifting grains dry the outer disk and lift volatile ices above water ice. Later, outward motion and refreezing push enrichment further past a shifting critical radius. Their runs leave solid carbon-to-oxygen and nitrogen-to-oxygen ratios near one beyond the most volatile ice lines, far above static-disk guesses, with the most volatile ices rising about a hundredfold.
arxiv-2604-14424: Mondal and Sarkar build a physics-based spatio-temporal surrogate for design, where costly detailed simulations bottleneck the process. Purely data-driven stand-ins run far faster than simulations but falter outside their training range. The team constrains a Koopman autoencoder model with the system's own physics, learning dynamics without intruding into the simulator. A second surrogate predicts how the Koopman operator behaves in a set time window under new conditions. The team evaluates the framework on two-dimensional incompressible flow around a cylinder.
arxiv-2604-14624: Vijayvargiya, Viswanathan, and Neubig study clarification in real software engineering tasks, where assistants must ask what users left unsaid. Not all missing information matters equally, and questions must target what users can realistically provide. Using Shapley values and distributional comparisons, they pin down two traits of good clarification: task relevance and user answerability. These properties become multi-stage reinforcement learning rewards training CLARITI, an 8-billion-parameter module matching GPT-5's issue-resolution rate on underspecified issues while asking 41 percent fewer questions.
arxiv-2604-14924: Liu, Schied, and Shen propose dynamic Lagrange multipliers for continuous-time portfolio selection with non-concave utility functions. Martingale duality dominates in complete markets, while dynamic programming can yield singular Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman solutions. Their multiplier function equals the value function's dual point, exactly its partial derivative with respect to wealth. The multiplier process shows scaling through optimal wealth and pricing kernels, reading as a moving shadow price under the envelope theorem. Classical optimal results are recovered and validated in tests on non-concave utility examples.
arxiv-2604-15024: Chen and nine others investigate nonlinear saturation of the toroidal Alfvén eigenmode from thermal effects with kinetic runs. In single-mode runs without zonal fields, saturation is governed by thermal effects above a drive ratio of 0.47 percent, with weak link to linear drive. Mode pitch falls as amplitude rises, driven by the phase-space zonal structure. It arrives when the mode merges into the continuum, with nearby harmonics separating and shift to energetic particle modes. With zonal fields, levels rise roughly twofold, showing zonal modes must be kept.
arxiv-2604-15324: Sultana and three colleagues test the struggle premium, the extra value people grant work that shows visible human effort, in an age of AI-made art. Surveying 70 students on process videos, time logs, written explanations, and flaws, they find process cues, above all videos and time spent, most shaped authenticity and value judgments. About 73 percent would pay more for human-made work, though effort cues also lifted AI-made work.
arxiv-2604-15724: Zaidi and three colleagues model charged-current muon neutrino deep inelastic scattering off argon-40 at DUNE energies. A fine-grained frame folds in Fermi motion, binding, nucleon links, meson gifts, and shadows across Bjorken x. Free nucleon shapes from MMHT 2014 sets, with NNLO QCD tweaks and target mass fixes, feed argon shapes from a relativistic nucleon spectral map in a local density view. The argon shapes then give scatter rates at 4 and 6 GeV beams, fit for DUNE and Fermilab short-baseline argon tests.
arxiv-2604-16024: Han and eight colleagues propose AstroVLM, a collaborative multi-agent system for diagnosing the quality of astronomical images. Astronomical imaging mixes many subtasks with tangled correlations, challenging quality checks and error localization even for NASA teams and expert enthusiasts. AstroVLM coordinates several agents to handle the multi-process task, drawing on knowledge from many fields. Tests on real-world imaging quality tasks show it beats all baselines, offering a reference for language models facing tangled multi-process tasks.
arxiv-2604-16624: Plueger and colleagues study how students reason about the CNOT gate. The CNOT gate matters because it entangles qubits. Through interviews on CNOT problems, they map students' CNOT toolbox of strategies and resources. They identify three resources: applying CNOT to states, describing its effect on the target given the control, and the idea that the control unchanged on basis states. Procedural use grounds the other two, which can sometimes mislead, and students deploy resources together. The study traces use with Dirac notation, superposition and entanglement in unproductive reasoning.
arxiv-2604-16824: Yan and colleagues propose SafeDream, a lightweight world-model framework for proactive early jailbreak detection. Multi-turn jailbreaks erode safety alignment across innocuous turns, succeeding over 90 percent of the time. Existing methods need costly weight changes, judge turns independently, and detect attacks only after harmful content appears. SafeDream encodes hidden states into a compact safety representation, accumulates weak risk signals, and rolls out attack and benign futures for early alarms. Across three benchmarks against 8 baselines, it detects attacks just over one turn before compliance with competitive false positive rates.
arxiv-2604-16924: Wang and twelve colleagues map how the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau, Earth's Third Pole, organizes climate links across the planet. They use a network analysis of observations and future projections. The study finds a persistent three-way pattern tying the plateau to the Arctic and Antarctica, casting it as a central climate integrator whose cascading risks current models largely overlook.
arxiv-2604-17224: Çakar, Raghu, and Zheng study the activation shape of tiny recursive models during unrolling. They find signals occupy a narrow subspace whose directions shift and can be tracked with power iterations. Weight-sharing focuses computation along a few dominant eigendirections, with focus varying sharply across sites. LASER maintains a low-rank basis via matrix-free tracking with a fidelity reset, cutting activation memory by about 60 percent with no real accuracy loss. The work raises questions about how recursive models allocate capacity during implicit reasoning.
arxiv-2604-17424: Devnani and Eyyunni disprove a recent conjecture of Ballantine and collaborators on the injectivity of a family of maps on integer partitions. The maps, called pre_k, come from applying elementary symmetric polynomials to partitions. The authors also offer a modified version of the conjecture and study how the maps relate to each other, rather than one at a time. They add alternate proofs for three subcases of the already-settled k-equals-2 case and discuss lower bounds for partitions in the image of pre_2.
arxiv-2604-17624: Dass and four colleagues introduce an AI-assisted text-to-model method for building models of procedural skills for tutoring. Building such representations by hand is a slow bottleneck for AI tutoring. Their method converts instructional materials to schema-complete Task-Method-Knowledge models through ontology-constrained prompting and templates, with experts kept in the loop. Applied to a graduate online AI course, it produced 23 models covering the full course for Ivy, an AI coach. Expert modeling time fell 50 to 70 percent, with models valid and highly reproducible.
arxiv-2604-18124: Weicheng Lin, Yi Zhang, Dang, and Liang-Jie Zhang present TLoRA, a fine-tuning method for large language models. It adjusts initialization and rank budgets together instead of one at a time. The adapter's A matrix starts from task-relevant directions found by singular value decomposition, then freezes while only B trains. Ranks are handed out by measured layer importance, cutting trainable parameters while holding strong results across reasoning, math, code, and chat tasks.
arxiv-2604-18224: Lei and 18 colleagues introduce WebCompass, a benchmark for judging language models that write, edit, and repair websites. Existing tests cover narrow slices, missing visual quality, interaction feel, and code-level thinking. It spans text, image, and video inputs with generation, editing, and repair tasks across seven groups from real work routines. Closed-source models lead overall, repair keeps pages working yet stays hard to run, and looks remain the hardest part, most of all for open models.
arxiv-2604-18524: Rajpurohit and four colleagues show light can induce orbital polarization in nickelates, where orbital freedom is usually idle across that transition. With a coupled multi-band model and live runs, they find light-driven transitions reduce nickel-site spin moments. Those transitions in effect suppress Hund's coupling in the excited state. Tuning the light makes them strongly orbital-picky, skewing shares. The new out-of-balance state turns unstable toward Jahn-Teller warps, driving settling along shared modes and opening a path to hidden phases with new order.
arxiv-2604-18824: Hibi, Kara, and Vien study, for each n, whether a tree on n nodes has a symmetric and unimodal independence polynomial. They also ask whether a symmetric and unimodal independence polynomial of degree n arises from a tree. The independence polynomial of a graph counts its independent sets by size. Symmetric means the coefficients read the same forwards and backwards, and unimodal means they rise and then fall.
arxiv-2604-19724: Zhang and four colleagues give the first theory for adversarial training under simple vision transformer architectures. When signal-to-noise ratio meets a stated rule and perturbation budgets stay modest, training drives robust training loss near zero with small robust error. Strong results persist despite overfitting, the benign overfitting seen only before in convolutional networks with adversarial training. Lab and real-world experiments back the theory.
arxiv-2604-19824: Ghinami and four colleagues present a framework that joins AFL++ with a stateful SystemC-TLM virtual prototype to fuzz embedded software true to life. Fuzzers work well for conventional software but struggle in embedded settings, where peripheral behavior matters. Older routes use fast user-mode simulators that drop peripheral realism, or full-system simulators with manual setup that limit large-scale use. Fuzzer-generated inputs are fed straight into the virtual prototype.
arxiv-2604-20224: Hsiao proves a compactness result for gradient Ricci solitons with scalar bounds and firm lower bounds on harmonic coordinates. His path lifts smoothness step by step through the soliton rule itself. As a payoff, any noncollapsed limit of such shapes has a smooth regular part, given bounded Ricci size. A steady gradient Ricci soliton also turns out cylindrical at far range when its Ricci curvature decays fast enough to sum.
arxiv-2604-20424: Mclean and four colleagues name three triggers of battery thermal runaway: falling local conductivity, heat capacity shifts, and intercalation heating. A multiscale frame links atomistic phonon math with grain-resolved thermal modeling to map large gradients across grain edges. Conductivity shifts trace to charge shifts and bond-strength changes, not to lithium rattler mechanics. Internal heating from intercalation breeds local gradients, finite-speed thermal wave clashes, and internal swings that strain the solid and break sub-grain regions, pointing to design rules for safer fast charging.
arxiv-2604-20924: Nie and colleagues build a sepsis early-warning tool that a doctor can follow rather than a black-box score. It first plays forward how a patient's vital signs may shift before onset, then flags risk from that path. One part tracks links across vital signs over time, one part feeds clinical cues into a language model, and a final part keeps forecasts within plausible body limits. Tests on two intensive-care data sets beat standard deep-learning and rule-based tools, while laying risk trends bare for clinicians.
arxiv-2604-21024: Mazouz and co-authors present a model and control plan for spacecraft in orbit aimed at tracking the Earth's Energy Imbalance. That metric is the net flux of radiation at the top of the atmosphere, a global yearly sum: sunlight minus infrared output. Precise tracking is hard because radiometers carry calibration errors. The team models an array of spherical craft, with shape and surface effects in view, and derives optimal control for spin rate. Matched attitudes aligned near the orbital normal sharpen detail in energy-gap gauging.
arxiv-2604-21124: Vincent Sprave and four colleagues unlock AMD's Versal AI Engine for mixed-criticality work, where tasks of different safety importance share one chip. Their runtime dispatcher moves jobs between processor tiles as the system's criticality mode changes, replacing fixed dataflow mappings. In a self-driving test it cut idle time by 65.5 percent, doubled throughput for low-criticality jobs, and added almost no execution overhead.
arxiv-2604-21224: Troy Porter, Igor Moskalenko, and Gudlaugur Johannesson ask whether the radio-infrared-gamma-ray link in star-forming galaxies reflects geometry rather than local cosmic-ray trapping. Synthetic views from 3D Milky Way models show a tight, near-linear correlation emerging from line-of-sight integration through the structured disc, even with no local calorimetry. The pattern survives moderate tilt but breaks edge-on. That makes scatter in the relation a diagnostic of galactic structure and cosmic-ray escape.
arxiv-2604-21424: Xinji Zeng and 12 colleagues show how to build tunable optical hopfions, 3D topological knots with poloidal and toroidal winding numbers, at any order. Mixes of Laguerre-Gaussian modes in free space give control of both winding numbers, shown up to orders 5 and 3 for a new state-of-the-art. The torus-knot shapes appear in tests via polarization filaments, confirming the topological textures. The work offers a route to hopfions of any order, with uses for topological photonics, optical communications, and condensed-matter analogies.
arxiv-2604-21524: Herbut and Ling point out an internal symmetry of the quadratic-band-touching Hamiltonian in a plane: the unitary symplectic group, like the Dirac case's orthogonal symmetry. All fermion bilinears fall into three small sets under this group. A coupled theory keeping this symmetry and rotations allows two interaction terms. When the interactions matter at low energies, it either holds or breaks into two smaller groups. On honeycomb lattices, symmetry to all orders in the momentum series equals the overlap of the symplectic and orthogonal groups, the unitary group.
arxiv-2604-21724: Chen and twelve colleagues propose X-GRAM, a frequency-aware way to scale language-model memory without scaling compute. Large token lookup tables waste parameters on rarely seen tokens and grow memory fast. X-GRAM compresses the long tail with hybrid hashing and alias mixing, then refines vectors to pull out local n-gram features. At sub-billion and just-over-billion scales, it gains up to 4.4 points over the plain backbone and about 3 points over strong retrieval baselines, with smaller tables.
arxiv-2604-21824: Le Fur and four colleagues propose a deterministic way to make bosonic grid states. Their circuits use only squeezing, displacement, and Kerr operations, and can be programmed as needed. Enforcing GKP symmetries gives states as good as current ones, but quality saturates with circuit depth. Instead, the circuits give phased-comb states. These are unitarily related to standard grid states with an intrinsic phase structure. Those states form a scalable error-correcting code with near-best results under boson loss, plus a universal gate set.
arxiv-2604-22024: Noerr and three colleagues build a model linking mitochondria movement, shape, and life cycle to a deformable axon edge. Traffic jams come from a push-and-pull between propulsion and crowding, with severity set by shape and stiffness. Elongated, stiff mitochondria stay in line and move fast, while bendy, squat mitochondria tend to jam and pile up. Fission makes jams worse by making crash-prone groups, while fusion restores transport by making anisotropic shapes that move through crowds with ease. Long jams strain the axon skin, causing dents and swelling.
arxiv-2604-22224: Chen and four colleagues use a physics-based pipe and AI framework to make propeller designs from performance targets. First, a store of over 20,000 propeller shapes comes with mock result curves. A Conditional Generation Model offers options from target thrust, power, and width. A Performance Prediction Model, a neural stand-in, predicts thrust, torque, and efficiency fast. A polish stage applies tuning to enforce thrust and bounds on blade-area ratio and thickness. Across settings, the framework makes designs matching targets while cutting round time versus expert-guided polish.
arxiv-2604-22724: Goikoetxea and Palacián teach goal-based control rules by copying paths made with optimization, not by gathering costly human examples. Their GCImOpt plan makes thousands of best paths in minutes on a laptop and grows the set by treating middle states as goals. The final rules stay small, win often, and run fast enough for on-board control chips.
arxiv-2604-22824: Zhang and three colleagues present WeatherSeg, a semi-supervised segmentation framework for cars that drive themselves in bad weather. It also cuts the cost of hand labels. A dual teacher-student model distills knowledge from weather-degraded images, while an attention mechanism retunes classifier weights to suit current conditions. Across clear, rainy, cloudy, and foggy scenes it beats baselines on accuracy and robustness. The result is a single approach to all-weather semantic segmentation for driving and related uses.
arxiv-2604-22924: Rantala simulates dense star clusters like early clusters seen by JWST, where runaway collisions can build supermassive stars. Near such stars, stellar black holes sink fast and interact strongly, becoming embedded in the stars' gaseous layers. This quasi-star phase far outlasts the supermassive star, allowing longer growth by collisions and embedded gravitational-wave sources if several black holes are captured. The sizes, masses, and nearby young blue clumps match the faint multiple Little Red Dots found by JWST.
arxiv-2604-23224: Thakur and Nandy run a fully numerical study of parametric resonance in quartic inflation during preheating, solving the coupled field equations without standard shortcuts. Their resonance patterns differ sharply from analytical treatments. At weak coupling, short modes settle into near-constant oscillations with saturating occupation numbers, while long modes grow slowly into a nonlinear oscillatory regime. Stronger coupling brings stochastic motion, with short modes showing staircase jumps in occupation number from production bursts and long modes growing steadily with only small fluctuations.
arxiv-2604-23724: Mao and nine colleagues present VIBES, a framework for spotting far-field anomalies in expressway surveillance video without drowning a vision-language model in full frames. A Bayesian module tracks normal motion from vehicle trajectories and fires triggers when motion deviates, so the model reasons only over selected frames and regions. Experiments show better far-field detection and interpretation at real-time speed across varied expressway scenes.
arxiv-2604-23824: Litschko, Plank, and Frassinelli show that simple statistical models beat large language models at inducing dictionaries for German dialects, a low-resource setting with wild spelling variation. Random forests trained on string-similarity features outperform a large open model, transfer across dialects, and stay lightweight. Using the induced dictionaries for query expansion lifts dialect retrieval scores by up to about 29 percent on one metric and 51 percent on another.
arxiv-2604-24024: Kawano, Miura, and Iwai break the linear scaling of multi-projector setup by embedding cameras in the target surface itself. The built-in cameras catch light from all projectors at once and split the patterns by incoming direction, so every projector's geometry can be solved together. Accuracy matches the old step-by-step method while capture cycles stay nearly flat as projectors are added.
arxiv-2604-24324: Helly and 17 colleagues release over 2.3 petabytes from FLAMINGO simulations. The suite's runs include cooling, star formation, mass loss, supernova feedback, and two forms of active galactic nucleus feedback. Products include snapshots, catalogues, maps, and power spectra. The set holds 22 hydrodynamical and 16 gravity-only simulations, including FLAMINGO-10k. Fiducial runs span three resolutions matching galaxy mass function and cluster gas fractions, while other runs vary cosmology and dark matter. A web service lets users explore and download datasets.
arxiv-2604-24924: Delepine and Khalil test the Left-Right Inverse Seesaw model through the decay tau to K pi nu-tau. In this model, TeV-scale right-handed neutrinos carry order-one Yukawa couplings while light neutrino masses stay protected by a violating scale. They identify a signal in the forward-backward CP asymmetry. They show the asymmetry is enhanced near K0-star-1430, reaching order 10 to the power minus 4, within reach of Belle II.
arxiv-2604-25124: Donohue and eight colleagues report on USEQIP, a two-week summer school in experimental quantum information processing. The school has run since 2009, paired with a summer internship program, to draw undergraduates from around the world into quantum research tools. The paper covers its structure, its hands-on lab work refined over many rounds and its outlook. It also tracks alumni careers, noting that many past students now contribute much to the quantum field.
arxiv-2604-25724: Prasad and Arora report a production deployment study of a modular inference architecture for compound AI systems. It was built at Salesforce for agent workflows such as Agentforce and code analysis with ApexGuru. Compound systems combine models, retrievers, and tools, demanding infrastructure that serves mixed, concurrent calls cheaply and quickly. Their platform uses serverless execution and dynamic autoscaling, plus machine-learning operations pipelines. Production results more than halved tail latency, raised throughput to almost four times the prior level, and cut costs by roughly a third.
arxiv-2604-25924: Verşebeniuc and six colleagues build a retrieval-augmented assistant for Maastricht University students facing bachelor project rules. Language models offer human-like answers to complex questions, but hallucination, missing facts, and context-specific accuracy remain problems in specialized domains. Their assistant grounds answers in up-to-date domain knowledge to raise accuracy and reliability. Tests with a robust evaluation framework and real-life trials show it meets student needs well. The work also points to open questions for LLM systems built for specific uses.
arxiv-2604-26024: Maxson and four colleagues fix bias in imbalanced classification with minority subconcepts. Class scores hide gaps across subconcepts in one class. Earlier scores favor larger minority subconcepts; true-label weighting helps, but such labels rarely exist at test time. The authors use predicted posteriors from a multi-class subconcept model. Weights are mean utility under that posterior, giving the soft predicted-weighted balanced accuracy (pBA) metric. On tabular, imaging, and text data, plain scores mislead in mixed classes, while pBA gives stabler reads.
arxiv-2604-26124: Ward and six colleagues report recent work on colliders. Their method improves infrared poles through amplitude-based resummation. It treats quantum electrodynamics and quantum chromodynamics jointly inside a larger gauge structure. It targets results precise enough for future machines. Uses span the Large Hadron Collider and its planned follow-up, linear machines, and other planned electron-positron machines, with new results and newly flagged issues for each setting.
arxiv-2604-26224: O'Brien studied weighted means from a positive Dunford-Schwartz operator on noncommutative Lp spaces, a setting where order of multiplication matters. He carried the classical subsequence argument into that setting and found many weighting sequences with a decay rule that the noncommutative individual ergodic theorem accepts as weights. The list covers sequences built from bounded independent draws and the Möbius function. Kindred results hold for T-admissible processes when the exponents meet a duality rule.
arxiv-2604-26424: Zapparoli and three colleagues built a two-stage stochastic scheduler for virtual power plants trading across energy and reserve markets under dynamic network tariffs. Detailed device and network limits join market and operational uncertainty, with conditional value-at-risk encoding risk appetite and Benders decomposition keeping large scenario sets tractable. Both cautious and bold strategies chased arbitrage, but risk aversion steadied profits by tracking physical dispatch more closely. Strong tariff signals cut expected profit by up to 65 percent with little extra flexibility gained.
arxiv-2604-26524: Bonança, Deffner, and Ingold traced Amir Caldeira's forty-year work on quantum Brownian motion. Starting from his early account of quantum Brownian motion, they stressed how dissipation changes tunneling out of a shaky state. They then followed his other routes past the Caldeira-Leggett model, through decoherence theory and quantum thermodynamics. The story shows how one physicist's frame kept shaping new fields across four decades.
arxiv-2604-26724: Li and six colleagues measure radial binary fraction profiles for 513 elliptical galaxies from the MaNGA survey, extending such studies beyond the Milky Way and its neighbors. After subtracting the effect of radial stellar-population variation, the median binary fraction turns approximately flat. For nearly all galaxies in the sample, the variation relative to the galaxy center at one effective radius stays under five percent. No clear link appears between the binary fraction gradient and stellar-population gradients, and UV-upturn and non-UV-upturn galaxies look comparable.
arxiv-2604-26924: Anderson and three colleagues test barium titanate films on silicon as a base for tunable acoustic resonators, filters for wireless bands. They excite symmetric Lamb modes in 120-nanometre membranes with a multi-cell electrode design that pairs strong coupling with workable impedance. Under DC bias, ferroelectric domains line up, letting voltage tune frequency and lift mode quality. The main resonance near 700 MHz shows a quality factor of 175 and coupling up to 25.1 percent, with modest series and parallel tuning.
arxiv-2604-27024: Bazarova and Alpay introduce the finite-horizon rank profile of a language: the smallest quantifier rank a first-order sentence needs to classify membership on words up to length n. They prove a rank calculus independent of regularity, bounding every language by ceiling log2 n plus 4. The supremum over n is finite exactly when the language is globally first-order definable, equaling the minimum rank of such a definition. For regular languages they prove a sharp gap: aperiodic monoids give bounded rank, others logarithmic rank.
arxiv-2604-27124: Sadashivaiah and three colleagues test sigmoid attention as a drop-in replacement for softmax attention in single-cell foundation models. Across six diverse single-cell datasets, sigmoid attention gives 25 percent higher cell-type separation, better cohesion, and lower validation loss, while training up to 10 percent faster. They trace the stability gain to bounded derivatives and a diagonal Jacobian structure, in contrast to the dense coupling of softmax, and stress-test large models without gradient clipping.
arxiv-2604-27724: Chen and seven colleagues propose MED-VRAG, an iterative multimodal retrieval system for medical question answering that reasons over document page images instead of OCR text. It couples patch-level page embeddings to a sharded MapReduce filter, scaling to about 350,000 pages with fast first-stage retrieval. A vision-language model then refines its query and banks evidence across up to three reasoning rounds. Across four medical benchmarks, MED-VRAG reaches 78.6 percent average accuracy, with retrieval adding about 6 points over no retrieval.
arxiv-2604-27824: Labib and three colleagues apply compressed sensing to gauge GHZ state fidelity, using their thinness to sharply reduce test load while keeping high care. They test the method on GHZ states using both quantum sims and Quantinuum's trapped-ion hardware. They add error catches during hardware tests, showing toughness and promise of compressed sensing for fidelity scores in noisy lab settings.
arxiv-2605-00024:
Ahmed Gamal Eldin presents evidence on the binding problem, the old puzzle of how scattered neural activity unifies into one conscious whole.
